cards.card_text: Balaam lifts up a second oracle, aimed right at Balak: “Arise, O Balak, and listen; give ear to me, O son of Zippor.” Friend, when somebody calls you by your full name and tells you to listen, that conversation is NOT going your way.

cards.card_text: Balaam lifts up an oracle and opens with a big introduction: Balaam son of Beor, a man whose eyes are open, who hears the words of God and sees a vision from the Almighty.
cards.verse_text: and he lifted up an oracle, saying: “This is the prophecy of Balaam son of Beor, the prophecy of a man whose eyes are open, the prophecy of one who hears the words of God, who sees a vision from the Almighty, who bows down with eyes wide open:

cards.card_text: So Balaam lifts up another oracle with the same kind of introduction, plus one new line: he has knowledge from the Most High.
cards.verse_text: Then Balaam lifted up an oracle, saying, “This is the prophecy of Balaam son of Beor, the prophecy of a man whose eyes are open, the prophecy of one who hears the words of God, who has knowledge from the Most High, who sees a vision from the Almighty, who bows down with eyes wide open:

cards.card_text: Once more Balaam lifts up an oracle: “Ah, who can live unless God has ordained it?”

cards.card_text: David says he's got an oracle in his heart about the transgression of the wicked man.
cards.verse_text: An oracle is in my heart regarding the transgression of the wicked man: There is no fear of God before his eyes.

cards.card_text: The people plotting against Jeremiah say the priest will still have the law, the wise will still have counsel and the prophet will still have an oracle.
cards.verse_text: Then some said, “Come, let us make plans against Jeremiah, for the law will never be lost to the priest, nor counsel to the wise, nor an oracle to the prophet.
